html:
Mahdia is a town on a narrow headland on the coast of Tunisia, founded in 916 by the first Fatimid caliph, Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi, as the fortified capital of his new state.

The Fatimids were an Ismaili Shia movement who had overthrown the Aghlabids in 909 with the help of Kutama Berbers. They chose a site easy to defend from sea and land, and built a great mosque and a harbour cut into the rock.

From Mahdia the Fatimids conquered Egypt in 969 and moved their capital to their new city of Cairo, leaving Ifriqiya to their Zirid governors. Mahdia stayed an important port, and was taken briefly by the Normans of Sicily in the 1100s.
